title: Justified lines with a code span come out loose
body:
`text::even_breaks` in `crates/acre/src/text.rs` breaks a justified paragraph by the method of Knuth and Plass. A line's badness is `100 r^3`, where `r` is the shortfall over the stretch of its spaces. Each space outside a code span may stretch by half its width (`STRETCH`), and no space shrinks. A last line of one word pays `LONE_WORD`.

Two faults show in a real figure:

- A line with a long code span, such as `` `care_bits[0]` has three 1s over each care character``, comes out very loose. Spaces in a code span never change width, so the few prose spaces on such a line take the whole shortfall.
- A paragraph ends on one short word, such as "bits.", "000." or "12945.".

## Proposal

- A prose space may shrink to about two thirds of its width, as in TeX. A line whose natural width passes `width` is a candidate when shrinking its spaces brings it inside, with badness `100 r^3` over the shrink. Spaces in code spans still never change.
- A last line shorter than about a third of `width` pays a penalty, so the breaker pulls a word or two down onto it. A paragraph that fits on one line pays nothing.
- Ragged text keeps the greedy breaker and does not move.
close_reason: Landed in df2b59e. Prose spaces in a justified line shrink to two thirds of their width (`SHRINK` in `text.rs`). A last line under a third of the width pays up to `SHORT_LAST_PENALTY`, which replaced `LONE_WORD`. A lone short last word can remain where pulling a word down would leave the line above very loose, such as "3." at width 500 in the Step 2 text of `figures/key-schemes.acre`.
